# Actions lockfile and Dependabot

The `verify-actions-lock` workflow runs `gh actions-lock --verify`. It fails when a workflow uses an unpinned action or when `.github/workflows/actions.lock` is out of sync with the workflows.

## The lockfile is optional for now

`actions.lock` has not been committed yet. The check passes without it as long as every third-party action is pinned to a full commit SHA. Committing the lockfile adds a second layer: each pin is re-verified upstream.

To create it, run these from a branch of this repo, then commit `.github/workflows/actions.lock`:

```
gh extension install github/gh-actions-lock
gh actions-lock
```

Do not edit the lockfile by hand.

## How Dependabot fits

Per GitHub's documentation ("Enforcing lockfiles for action dependencies"), when Dependabot bumps an action it regenerates the matching lockfile entry in the same pull request. No extra workflow or configuration is needed beyond `.github/dependabot.yml` managing `github-actions`.

Two caveats from the same documentation:

- Dependabot does not add a workflow that has no lockfile entries yet. The first lockfile has to be generated by a person, as above. After that, Dependabot keeps it current.
- The lockfile is regenerated by `gh actions-lock`, so any workflow change that adds or removes a `uses:` dependency needs the command re-run (or a Dependabot bump) before `verify` goes green.

## What was deliberately not added

A custom workflow that re-runs `gh actions-lock` and pushes to Dependabot PRs. It would need `contents: write`, pushes made with `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger other checks, and gh-actions-lock is a technical preview whose flags may change. Revisit if Dependabot's own handling proves insufficient.
